content.title: Dual System Collision | Rule Validation
content.summary: First establish independent rules for the two opposing systems, and then let them converge to form a lasting third state.

quick_start.input_format: System A materials/rules + System B materials/rules + separately established + a convergence collision + the third state formed by both parties
quick_start.recommended_input: On the left side of the experimental platform is liquid glass that crystallizes, and on the right side is magnetic sand that pulsates; after proving their respective rules, they only converge once to form a suspended lattice that is simultaneously transparent and continuously pulsating.
required_anchors: The two systems are first established independently
Material or movement rules are clearly different
The third state preserves the evidence of both parties at the same time
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: First establish independent rules for the two opposing systems, and then let them converge to form a lasting third state.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Establish two systems separately with distinct color, material physics, motion cadence and starting zones. Alternate equal proof beats while their spatial distance decreases, align them on one readable axis, permit exactly one convergence event, and end on a third shared result that neither system produced alone.

invariants.rule: Give each system an independent establishing proof.
invariants.purpose: Prevents color alone from carrying identity.
invariants.ablation_failure: Immediate collision makes the systems interchangeable.

invariants.rule: Keep material physics and cadence distinct before convergence.
Reduce one visible spatial gap across matched views.
invariants.ablation_failure: Random angles obscure whether convergence is approaching.

invariants.rule: Allow only one terminal meeting event.

invariants.purpose: Proves both inputs affected the result.
invariants.ablation_failure: A flash followed by reset provides no outcome evidence.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original subject or system whose identity remains stable.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One visible variable that changes in countable causal stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained behavior rule that makes the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: A coherent information order that does not copy source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: One clean physical or graphic consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: A new hierarchy of diegetic cues supporting state changes.

anti_copy_exclusions: weapons, petals and the source mid-air collision pose
